upstream_issue.title: Serious Issues with Real-Time Streaming
upstream_issue.closure_reason: not_planned/inactive rather than documented technical resolution
upstream_issue.reported_behavior: long-running streaming processing time increases and quality degrades because all audio observed since stream start is repeatedly supplied to inference

source_direct_findings: ASRStreamingState initializes an ever-growing audio_accum buffer.
For every full streaming chunk, the official implementation appends the new chunk to audio_accum.
The implementation documentation explicitly states that each incremental decode step re-feeds all audio seen so far to the model.
The actual vLLM input binds state.audio_accum as the audio payload on every decode step.
finish_streaming_transcribe also appends the tail to the accumulated audio and supplies the full accumulated audio again.

Upstream issue #148 reports long-session slowdown/unresponsiveness and quality degradation from this same accumulation mechanism; the issue was closed as inactive/not-planned, not with a documented source fix.
Current official main still contains the all-audio re-feed implementation at the observed source blob.
project_inferences_not_runtime_facts: Because the amount of audio presented at decode step n grows with elapsed conversation duration, the amount of re-presented audio across successive chunks grows superlinearly in session length in the absence of an effective hidden cache. This is a complexity/risk inference, not measured clay-direct-dev runtime scaling.
A short streaming demo PASS cannot establish Frankenstein's required long-conversation behavior; latency slope, resource slope and transcript stability over time must be measured explicitly.

The existing LOCAL-SOLO voice acceptance ladder should treat Qwen3-ASR native vLLM streaming as unpromoted until long-session behavior is measured at fixed chunk sizes on the actual resident Frankenstein resource envelope.

counterhypotheses.statement: vLLM or model-internal multimodal caching may substantially amortize repeated audio processing despite the growing source payload.
A bounded rolling audio window could cap the long-session cost while preserving acceptable German transcript continuity.
counterhypotheses.risk: windowing changes context/rollback semantics and may create boundary errors, duplicated text or lost words

conditions: identical German fixture sequence and non-speech strata
measure at cumulative stream ages such as 1, 5, 10, 20 and 30 minutes
record per-chunk decode latency p50/p95/p99 and latency-versus-stream-age slope
record RSS/VRAM and GPU utilization versus stream age
record partial transcript stability, duplicated/replayed text and endpoint/cancellation correctness
compare official unbounded accumulation against a separately labelled bounded-window experimental challenger only after baseline measurement
do not grant V4/V6 credit from source evidence

next_exact_action: Extend the already-owned T7-ASR-004 target benchmark, after the current pinned German comparator/non-speech gate, with a no-restart long-session streaming slope test. Baseline the official unbounded accumulation path first; only then test a bounded-window challenger. Persist raw per-chunk timings and resource traces.
